answer.short: An upward-opening curve with $x$-intercepts $-\frac12$ and $\frac32$, $y$-intercept $-2$, and minimum $\left(\frac12,-3\right)$.
answer.worked:
Horizontally dilate by a factor of $\frac12$: halve every $x$-coordinate and retain each $y$-coordinate.
$$\begin{align*}(x,y)&\mapsto\left(\frac{x}{2},y\right)\\x\text{-intercepts}&=-\frac12,\ \frac32\\y\text{-intercept}&=-2\\\text{minimum}&=\left(\frac12,-3\right)\end{align*}$$
Sketch a smooth curve through these points, retaining the upward-opening shape and continuation arrows.

answer.short: An upward-opening curve with $x$-intercepts $-1$ and $3$, $y$-intercept $-6$, and minimum $(1,-9)$.
answer.worked:
Vertically dilate by a factor of $3$: triple every $y$-coordinate and retain each $x$-coordinate.
$$\begin{align*}(x,y)&\mapsto(x,3y)\\x\text{-intercepts}&=-1,\ 3\\y\text{-intercept}&=3(-2)=-6\\\text{minimum}&=(1,3(-3))=(1,-9)\end{align*}$$
Sketch a smooth curve through these points, retaining the upward-opening shape and continuation arrows.

answer.worked:
Horizontally dilate by a factor of $\frac13$ and vertically dilate by a factor of $2$.
$$\begin{align*}(x,y)&\mapsto\left(\frac{x}{3},2y\right)\\x\text{-intercepts}&=-\frac13,\ \frac33=1\\y\text{-intercept}&=2(-2)=-4\\\text{minimum}&=\left(\frac13,2(-3)\right)=\left(\frac13,-6\right)\end{align*}$$
Sketch a smooth curve through these points, retaining the upward-opening shape and continuation arrows.

answer.worked:
Horizontally dilate by a factor of $\frac1\pi$ and vertically dilate by a factor of $\pi$.
$$\begin{align*}(x,y)&\mapsto\left(\frac{x}{\pi},\pi y\right)\\x\text{-intercepts}&=-\frac1\pi,\ \frac3\pi\\y\text{-intercept}&=\pi(-2)=-2\pi\\\text{minimum}&=\left(\frac1\pi,\pi(-3)\right)=\left(\frac1\pi,-3\pi\right)\end{align*}$$
Sketch a smooth curve through these points, retaining the upward-opening shape and continuation arrows.
